subject: Startups
title: Netflix: DVDs to Streaming
description: A 60-second lesson on Netflix: DVDs to Streaming.

hook.text: Netflix mailed DVDs in red envelopes for a decade. Then it bet everything on a technology nobody was ready for.

buildup.text: Reed Hastings saw that broadband was getting faster and cheaper. He knew physical media had an expiration date.

discovery.text: Netflix launched streaming in 2007 with a tiny catalog. DVD revenue still dwarfed it, but Hastings doubled down.

twist.text: Blockbuster had its own streaming service too—but killed it because executives feared cannibalizing store revenue.

climax.text: Netflix now has over 260 million subscribers. The company that mailed discs became the king of streaming.

punchline.text: Red envelopes became red play buttons. Timing was everything.

quiz.question: Why did Blockbuster kill its own streaming service?
